kicker: Market valuation · Sensex earnings vs price, Oct 2021–Oct 2026
title: Sensex earnings rose 11% in a year. The index fell 11%.
dek: Trailing Sensex EPS rose 10.7% to ₹3,742 in the year to October 2026, while the index fell 11.3% to 74,460. The trailing P/E dropped from 24.8x to 19.9x as foreign investors sold a net ₹2.95 lakh cr of equities.

chart.title: Sensex trailing EPS and index level, end-October each year
chart.sub: columns: trailing 12-month consolidated EPS (₹) · line: Sensex close, end-October

read: This year's fall came from a lower multiple, not lower profits: the index now costs a fifth less per rupee of earnings than a year ago.
sources: BSE Sensex closing levels; Sensex trailing consolidated EPS; NSDL/CDSL FPI flow data; consensus forward estimates; Vantage analysis
notes: Index levels are Sensex closes at end-October each year (30 Oct 2026 was the month's last trading day). Trailing EPS is 12-month consolidated earnings per index unit; it equals the index level divided by the trailing P/E (74,460 ÷ 19.9x), so the five-year EPS growth is 82% (12.7% a year) against 26% for the index (4.7% a year). P/E series built on other EPS bases, such as those published by data vendors, read higher (about 21x in November 2026) but show the same fall. The forward P/E uses consensus 12-month-forward earnings estimates, which are forecasts and get revised. Foreign flows are net equity flows from depository data for January–October 2026 (₹34,843 cr in October); early-November tallies ranged from ₹2.95 to about ₹3.1 lakh cr depending on the cut-off and whether primary-market buying is netted.
